main_text.head: DE CLAMORE AD DEVM, seu de Supplicationibus publicis.
main_text.p: In Regis Assyriorum edicto, tertium in numero τῶν πρακτῶν[?] locum supplicationes publicae sibi vendicant.

Clament ad Deum fortiter. Requiritur autem hac parte edicti, ut non solum singuli votis cordis, gemitibus, suspirijs, lacrymis agant, sed etiam ad alios excitandos & exacuedos, voce clarissima preces cō-cipiant, omnesq; uno ore & Spiritu commune negocii agant.

Δέησις[?] Paulo est supplicatio, qua petimus à Deo, ut vel ab moleftijs quae nos graviter premunt liberet, vel ab impendentibus malis praefervet. 1.Tim.2.1. Facit huc illud Iacobi 5.16. Confiteminia-lij alijs offensas, & orate alij pro alijs, ut sanemini: multū enim valet deprecatio iusti assidua[?].
Cognatum ei vocabulum ἱκετηρία[?] est, quod exstat Hebr.5.7. Christus cū in diebus carnis suae, deprecationes & supplicationes, δεήσεως τε καὶ ἱκετηρίας[?], apud eum qui po-

page.notes: Greek words are uncertain: "τῶν πρακτῶν" in the first Greek phrase, the word opening the Paulo paragraph (possibly Δέησις), and the Greek at the end of the last paragraph. The phrase "Confiteminia-lij alijs" is printed this way and may be a printing error for "Confitemini alijs". The word "assidua" is printed "afsidua" (long s as f) and is read as assidua. The word "terat" at the foot right is the catchword completing "po-terat" on the next page. Long s was normalised to s throughout. Italic and Greek marks are approximate.
